info.title: Node Normalization
info.description:
Node Normalization takes a CURIE, and returns:
  1. The preferred CURIE for this entity
  2. All other known equivalent identifiers for the entity
  3. Semantic types for the entity as defined by the Biolink Model
This is the Elasticsearch-backed implementation of the Node Normalization API, maintained by the BioThings group at Scripps Research (source code). The data it serves is created by Babel, which finds identifier equivalences and makes sure that CURIE prefixes are Biolink Model compliant. To determine whether Node Normalization is likely to be useful for the CURIEs you are interested in, please check /get_semantic_types, which lists the Biolink semantic types for which normalization has been attempted. The semantics of each endpoint are described in the Node Normalization API documentation. To learn more about how Babel creates cliques of equivalent identifiers, read its documentation.

get.summary: Status information on this NodeNorm instance
get.description: Returns service status and version information for this NodeNorm instance. Babel discovery runs at startup and every 600 seconds in the background, independently of incoming requests. It uses the configured Elasticsearch client and requires no configured version list. Successful discovery publishes the release registry and query indices together. Moving the configured default alias takes effect on the next successful refresh without restarting; each in-flight request keeps its selected concrete indices. The default uses every exact concrete backing index of its configured alias, including older builds, and has no separate Babel configuration override. Explicit selection of the default version uses those same targets. Other releases select the newest valid mappings._meta.build_date, compared in UTC with naive timestamps treated as UTC; missing or malformed dates rank below valid dates and ties use index name descending. Adding a release does not automatically change the default. Discovery has a 10-second total deadline; failure retains the previous snapshot and checked_at timestamp, exposes refresh_error, and retries after 30 seconds. Separate health checks validate the expected Babel source version on every default index, with a 3-second deadline, a 5-second success cache and a 1-second failure cache. Concurrent status requests share a health check. A changed default version or indices triggers a new check. Health failure returns HTTP 503. All status responses send Cache-Control: no-store.

deployment_environment.description: Explicit deployment environment loaded at startup from NODENORM_DEPLOYMENT_ENV or the deployment_environment JSON configuration field. Set NODENORM_DEPLOYMENT_ENV=local for local runs. Kubernetes supplies the environment variable from the gov.nih.ncats.appenv pod label, whose deployed values are CI, Prod, and Test. Capitalization is preserved. Defaults to unknown when unset; it is not inferred from request headers or hostnames.

babel_version.description: Temporary compatibility field for existing clients. Always equals babel.default_version; new clients should use the babel object for multi-release metadata.

babel_version_url.description: Temporary compatibility field for existing clients. Always equals babel.available_versions[babel.default_version], the default release URL.

backend.description: Backend identifier retained for compatibility with existing clients' API version tracking. Does not select a Babel release.

biolink_model_toolkit_version.description: Biolink Model version used by the toolkit.

default_version.description: Babel release used when babel_version is omitted. Its release URL is available under the matching key in babel.available_versions.

available_versions.description: Babel release names mapped to their release URLs. Releases are resolved from Elasticsearch metadata. The default uses its alias targets; other releases select the newest metadata build date when duplicate builds exist. This map does not indicate backend health.

indices.description: Babel release names mapped to arrays of concrete Elasticsearch indices selected by the latest successful discovery snapshot, refreshed every 600 seconds in the background. Has the same release keys as babel.available_versions. The default preserves every exact alias target even if older than other builds; explicit requests for the default version use those same targets. Other releases select one index by newest valid metadata build_date, with index name descending as the final tie-break. Requests keep their selected targets throughout processing. This map does not indicate backend health. Example index names are illustrative.

checked_at.description: UTC time of the last successful Babel discovery. Retained when a refresh fails; separate health checks do not change it.

refresh_error.description: Present after a failed background discovery. The last valid registry remains active and discovery retries after 30 seconds. Cleared by a successful refresh. Contains no upstream connection details.

errors.description: Optional discovery errors keyed by release name. Selecting an affected release returns HTTP 503; the release is excluded from both babel.available_versions and babel.indices. Duplicate builds are resolved deterministically rather than reported as errors.

example.2026aug1: No index metadata identifies Babel release 2026aug1

503.description: The default Elasticsearch health check failed or exceeded its 3-second deadline. Failed checks are cached for 1 second; an expired success is not served after failure.

get.summary: The git commit this instance was built from
get.description: Returns the git commit hash of the deployed code. For the API version, see `version` in /status.

get.summary: Get the equivalent identifiers and semantic types for the curie(s) entered.
get.description: Returns the equivalent identifiers and semantic types for the curie(s). Each input CURIE maps to a normalized node, or to `null` if it is unknown. The boolean flags accept `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off`, `t`/`f` and `y`/`n`, in any case; any other value is a 400.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: Whether to return curie descriptions when possible

parameters.name: individual_types
parameters.description: Whether to return individual types for equivalent identifiers

200.description: A normalized node (or `null`) for every input CURIE

400.description: No `curie` parameter was supplied, or a flag is not a boolean. An unknown, removed, or malformed babel_version returns 400 with the available release names.

post.summary: Get the equivalent identifiers and semantic types for the curie(s) entered.
post.description: Returns the equivalent identifiers and semantic types for the curie(s). Use the `conflate` and `drug_chemical_conflate` flags to choose which conflations to apply. Select a Babel release with the optional babel_version string in the JSON body. Omitting it uses the configured default release.

200.description: A normalized node (or `null`) for every input CURIE

400.description: The body is not a JSON object, has no `curies`, or a flag is not a boolean. An unknown, removed, or malformed babel_version returns 400 with the available release names.

get.summary: Normalize and deduplicate a set of identifiers and return a single hash that represents this set.
get.description: Returns the set ID for a given set of CURIEs. A set ID is an identifier that can be used to identify this set of CURIEs going forward. It is currently impossible to recreate a set of CURIEs from a set ID, but the same set of CURIEs given to the same version of Node Normalization will always return the same set ID.

parameters.name: conflation
parameters.description: Set of conflations to apply; see /get_allowed_conflations

200.description: The set ID for the input CURIEs

400.description: No `curie` parameter was supplied. An unknown, removed, or malformed babel_version returns 400 with the available release names.

post.summary: Normalize and deduplicate several sets of identifiers and return a hash for each set.
post.description: Returns one set ID per input set, keyed by the set's position in the request as a string ("0", "1", ...). Select one Babel release for the entire batch with the optional babel_version query parameter.

200.description: One set ID per input set, keyed by its index

400.description: The body is not a non-empty JSON array of objects. An unknown, removed, or malformed babel_version returns 400 with the available release names.

get.summary: Return a list of Biolink semantic types for which normalization has been attempted.
get.description: Returns the distinct Biolink classes found in the index, together with all of their ancestors.

200.description: The semantic types in this instance

400.description: Invalid request. An unknown, removed, or malformed babel_version returns 400 with the available release names.

get.summary: Return a list of named conflations.
get.description:
Returns the conflations this instance can apply. Conflation combines cliques on the fly:
  1. GeneProtein merges protein-coding genes with the proteins they encode. The gene(s) always appear first in the combined clique.
  2. DrugChemical merges chemicals based on their active ingredient. The active ingredient appears before any formulations in the combined clique.
You can read more about conflation in the Babel documentation.

head.summary: Check that the list of named conflations is available.
head.description: The headers of `GET /get_allowed_conflations`, without the body.

BabelVersion.name: babel_version
BabelVersion.description: Babel release name discovered from Elasticsearch metadata. Omit to use the default release; unknown, removed, or malformed values return HTTP 400 with the available release names. Ambiguous releases return HTTP 503; /status reports discovery errors.
Babel release used for this response. Exposed to browser clients through Access-Control-Expose-Headers.

UnsupportedBabelVersion.description: Invalid request, including an unknown, removed, or malformed babel_version. Selector errors include the available release names discovered from Elasticsearch metadata.

BabelReleaseUnavailable.description: Processing failed or the selected Babel release is unavailable. HTTP 503 indicates an unavailable release; see babel.errors in /status. Requests never fall back to a different release.
